reader.requirement: At --std 85 sequential access to a relative file (sequential access mode, or READ NEXT in dynamic mode) returns only existing records in ascending relative record number, skipping deleted and never-written numbers, and updates the RELATIVE KEY item when one is declared.
reader.edition-search: grep Edition/DialectBehaviors in RelativeConnector.cs: the only use is Write's out-of-range key arm; ReadSequential, ReadNext and Start consult no edition. KeyedConnector.OpenCore's positioning has no edition test either.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf19_06 and g85_bf21_05 cover gaps from out-of-order random writes; not deleted records, variable-length records, a large RRN, or READ NEXT after a START or after a random READ (probed here).

probes.expected: ascending RRN of existing records (7 deleted), RELATIVE KEY set to each RRN

probes.printed: RDY AFTER START>4 010 [0010  ] / RDY NEXT 999 [999LLL] / RDY KEY 1 00 [ONE   ] / RDY NEXT AFTER RANDOM 004 [00004 ]
probes.expected: after START GREATER 4 the next existing record is 10, then 999 (the largest 3-digit key); after a random READ of 1, NEXT gives 4

citations.check: OK  §1985:VIII.2.4.4 GR2  (2.4.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR2

reader.notes: The relative store is keyed by RRN, so ReadSequential walks keys in ascending order and a deleted slot is absent. A dynamic READ NEXT after a random READ continues from the record that READ returned.

refuter.evidence: r42-002 (--std 85), records at RRN 2,5,9,12: dynamic READ NEXT gives 2, then after MOVE 11 TO the RELATIVE KEY item the next READ NEXT gives 5 (the key item does not position a format 1 READ, §1985:VIII.4.5.4 GR4 d); a random DELETE of 9 then READ NEXT gives 12 (deleted record skipped); a random WRITE of 3 behind the position then READ NEXT gives 10 at end; a failed random READ (23) then READ NEXT gives 46 (§1985:VIII.4.5.4 GR12); START EQUAL 3 then READ NEXT gives 3; START NOT LESS 6 then READ NEXT gives 12; sequential access with RELATIVE KEY: MOVE 9999 then MOVE 1 to the key between READs has no effect, the reads give 2,3,5,12 with the key set to each RRN, then 10. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VIII.2.4.4 GR2  (2.4.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR2'; 'OK  §1985:VIII.4.5.4 GR4'; 'OK  §1985:VIII.4.5.4 GR12'. Grep of RelativeConnector.cs for DialectBehavior: only Write's key-out-of-range arm.
